claim: The Standard Model of particle physics describes three of the four fundamental forces and classifies all known elementary particles
The Higgs boson was experimentally confirmed at CERN in 2012 validating the mechanism that gives particles mass
Quarks are elementary particles that combine in groups of two or three to form hadrons such as protons and neutrons
The strong nuclear force binds quarks together into protons and neutrons and is mediated by gluons
Neutrinos are nearly massless particles that interact only via the weak force and gravity passing through ordinary matter almost undetected
Antimatter consists of particles with the same mass but opposite charge to their matter counterparts
The electromagnetic spectrum ranges from radio waves to gamma rays with visible light occupying a narrow band between 380 and 700 nanometers
Superconductivity occurs when certain materials cooled below a critical temperature conduct electricity with zero resistance
Bose-Einstein condensates form when bosonic particles are cooled to near absolute zero causing them to occupy the same quantum state
The photoelectric effect demonstrated that light consists of discrete quanta called photons as explained by Einstein in 1905
Wave-particle duality means all matter exhibits both wave-like and particle-like properties depending on the experiment
Quantum tunneling allows particles to pass through energy barriers that classical physics would consider impenetrable
The Pauli exclusion principle states that no two identical fermions can occupy the same quantum state simultaneously
Thermodynamic entropy measures the number of microscopic configurations corresponding to a macroscopic state
The second law of thermodynamics states that the total entropy of an isolated system can only increase over time
Special relativity predicts that time passes more slowly for objects moving at high velocities relative to a stationary observer
Mass and energy are equivalent as expressed by E equals mc squared meaning mass can be converted to energy and vice versa
Gravitational lensing occurs when massive objects bend light from distant sources as predicted by general relativity
Neutron stars are the collapsed remnants of massive stars with densities exceeding a billion tonnes per cubic centimeter
Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars that emit beams of electromagnetic radiation detectable as periodic pulses
The Hubble constant describes the rate at which the universe is expanding currently estimated at approximately 70 km per second per megaparsec
Dark energy constitutes approximately 68 percent of the total energy density of the universe and drives accelerating expansion
The Big Bang theory describes the expansion of the universe from an extremely hot dense initial state approximately 13.8 billion years ago
Exoplanets are planets orbiting stars other than the Sun with over 5000 confirmed as of 2023
The habitable zone is the region around a star where conditions could allow liquid water to exist on a planetary surface
Supermassive black holes with millions to billions of solar masses exist at the center of most large galaxies
The Milky Way galaxy contains an estimated 100 to 400 billion stars and is approximately 100000 light-years in diameter
Nuclear fusion powers stars by converting hydrogen into helium releasing enormous amounts of energy
Plasma is the fourth state of matter consisting of ionized gas and constitutes over 99 percent of visible matter in the universe
The Doppler effect causes the observed frequency of a wave to change when the source and observer move relative to each other
